component.name: Mithrandir
component.summary: System cleaner, optimizer and power manager

description.p: Mithrandir is a high-performance system maintenance suite, deep cache cleaner, and hardware power utility written in Rust with GTK4 and Libadwaita. It delivers instantaneous cleanup scans, cache pruning, hardware power management, and granular control over startup services and system processes without background resource overhead. (Independent project; not affiliated with or endorsed by CachyOS, GNOME, or Debian.)

Designed with a focus on safety and transparency, Mithrandir protects critical operating system paths, respects user sandboxes, and runs diagnostic telemetry off the main UI thread for stutter-free operation.

ul.li: High-Throughput Cleaner: Multi-threaded cleanup for package caches, thumbnails, application logs, and Flatpak caches
Kernel & BORE Scheduler Control: Runtime and persistent sysctl management for the BORE CPU scheduler
Hardware Power Profiles: Coordinated CPU Turbo Boost, scaling governors, EPP power profiles, and PCIe ASPM management
Pure Rust System Tray: StatusNotifierItem and DBusMenu panel integration adapting automatically to Light and Dark desktop themes
Zero-Sleep Real-Time Telemetry: Instant CPU delta calculation, dual GPU metrics, and battery health reporting
Debounced Smart Boost: Safe one-click memory optimization and temporary file reclamation
Adaptive Libadwaita Interface: Responsive layout conforming to GNOME HIG on desktop and mobile screens

description.p: Permissions: Mithrandir manages the system it runs on, so this package does not keep it in a sandbox. It runs every action (cache cleaning, systemd services, GRUB, BTRFS snapshots, power and kernel settings, uninstalling software) on your computer through flatpak-spawn, with your normal user privileges, and asks for your password through polkit when an action needs root. It can read and write your whole home directory and the data of your other Flatpak apps in ~/.var/app, so it can clean their caches.

The AI assistant sends a summary of your system to the provider you choose (a cloud API, or a local model server) and can propose a shell command. When you click Execute Fix or Apply Fix, that command runs on your computer the same way, and as root after a password prompt when it uses sudo. Read a proposed command before running it.
